title: Antiferromagnetism-altered plasmon dynamics
authors: Yifan Su, Suheng Xu, Rocco A. Vitalone, Ziyu Liu, Emil Viñas Boström, Na Wu, Chun-Ying Huang, Zhuquan Zhang, Jaehoon Jung, Daniel G. Chica, Vinícius da Silveira Lan Avelar, Yiping Wang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, James C. Hone, Xiaoyang Zhu, Cory R. Dean, Xavier Roy, Angel Rubio, D. N. Basov
abstract: The interaction between plasmons and magnons is a long-sought phenomenon with implications for fundamental physics and spintronics applications. In three-dimensional systems, this coupling is suppressed by the large mismatch in energy scales, but two-dimensional (2D) plasmons with gapless dispersion can overlap with magnons over a broad spectral range. Despite numerous theoretical predictions, experimental observation of magnon-plasmon interaction has remained elusive. In this work, we study a first-of-its-kind hybrid plasmon-magnon platform based on 2D materials. By deploying scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM) with terahertz radiation, we image propagating plasmon wavepackets at a graphene/NiPS$_3$ interface and track their dynamics across the antiferromagnetic transition of NiPS$_3$. We observe a clear renormalization of the plasmon-polariton dispersion concurrent with the onset of antiferromagnetic order. With complementary Raman scattering and nano-terahertz spectroscopy, we unveil spectral weight redistribution and dielectric screening changes, potentially associated with the multi-magnon continuum, as the underlying mechanism. These results provide solid evidence of coupling between plasmon and antiferromagnetic order, marking a cornerstone for a potential platform for hybrid magnon-plasmon interactions in 2D materials, opening avenues for coherent spin-plasmon devices and tunable terahertz spintronic components.
summary: This paper reports on the experimental observation of coupling between plasmons and antiferromagnetic order in a graphene/$	ext{NiPS}_3$ heterostructure. Using terahertz s-SNOM, the authors tracked plasmon dynamics and found that the plasmon dispersion renormalizes precisely when the underlying material enters an antiferromagnetic state. This establishes a novel platform for developing coherent spin-plasmon devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the elusive interaction between plasmons (collective electron oscillations) and magnons (spin waves) in low-dimensional magnetic systems.
main_result: The researchers observed a clear renormalization of the plasmon-polariton dispersion coinciding with the onset of antiferromagnetic order, providing evidence of plasmon-magnon coupling.
method: The work combines advanced experimental techniques like terahertz s-SNOM with theoretical modeling (DFT) to probe the coupled dynamics.
model_or_system: The platform is a hybrid system consisting of a graphene monolayer placed on top of a $	ext{NiPS}_3$ microcrystal, which acts as a 2D antiferromagnet.
key_observables: Plasmon-polariton dispersion, plasmon wavepacket dynamics, spectral weight redistribution, and the renormalization of the plasmon-polariton velocity across the antiferromagnetic transition temperature ($T_N$).
important_parameters: The system operates in the 2D limit, utilizing terahertz radiation, and the key transition is the antiferromagnetic ordering temperature ($T_N \approx 155 	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis initially rules out direct magnon-plasmon hybridization based on the observed increase in plasmon velocity, suggesting dielectric screening changes are the dominant mechanism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the device structure, the comparison of excitation energy scales, and spacetime maps showing the measured plasmon-polariton velocity increasing across the antiferromagnetic transition temperature.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical motivation for plasmon-magnon coupling, details the $	ext{Graphene}/	ext{NiPS}_3$ platform, presents s-SNOM measurements tracking plasmon dynamics across $T_N$, and interprets these results via spectral analysis.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the coupling between electronic excitations (plasmons) and magnetic order (magnons) in a tunable 2D platform, which is a cornerstone problem in emergent magnetoplasmonics and open quantum systems.
